newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo's Trepca closing for August overhaul - agency.
newsitem.headline: Yugo's Trepca closing for August overhaul - agency.

text.p: Yugoslavia's Rudarsko Metalurski Kombinat Trepca will close down all of its plants for overhaul in August, Tanjug news agency reported on Tuesday.
The overhaul of lead, zinc and power plants will be completed by the end of the month and should secure conditions for doubling the plant's production, the report said.
The main furnace in the lead plant is also out of operation.
Trepca has produced 40,000 tonnes of lead since February 1995 and expects output of another 60,000 tonnes by the year-end, the report said.
In 1996, Trepca's export earnings stood at $94 million.

According to an earlier Serbian Chamber of Commerce report, Trepca plans to increase its 1997 production of ore and concentrate by 167 percent, refined lead by 126.9 percent and electrolytic zinc by 142.5 percent on the previous year.
Trepca signed a five-year $519 million deal with Greek metals trading firm Mitileneos in May this year.

The plant will supply its Greek partner with lead and zinc metal worth $350 million over the next five years, while Mitileneos will provide Trepca with lead and zinc concentrate worth $150 million and mining equipment and spare parts worth $19 million.

The Trepca group, based in Serbia's southern province of Kosovo, consists of 14 lead and zinc mines, nine flotation and two metallurgy plants and 14 factories. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 311 4254
